newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico unveils plan to boost reserves, assure mkts.
newsitem.headline: Mexico unveils plan to boost reserves, assure mkts.

text.p: Banco de Mexico on Wednesday unveiled a new strategy to build reserves and dampen exchange rate volatility, via increased dollar put auctions or dollar sales.

It said the joint central bank-Finance Ministry Exchange Commission decided it would auction an additional $300 million of dollar put options if, by the 16th of each month, 80 percent or more of existing options had been exercised.
It said the additional options auctioned would only be valid for the rest of the month. The first additional auction would be held on February 21.

"The favorable conditions of the balance of payments have improved further during this year, partly for seasonal reasons, which offers an opportunity to accelerate the pace of accumulation of reserves without upsetting the exchange market," the central bank statement said.

It said higher reserves also enabled it to introduce a scheme to soften exchange rate volatility, via the sale of $200 million to banks when the dollar rises against the peso more than two percent on any day.

"In case the (dollar) exchange rate rises on a given day by more than two percent from the exchange rate of the previous working day, $200 million will be auctioned among banks with a minimum price two percent above (the exchange rate) on the prior working day," it said.
The move would calm nervous markets by adding liquidity, it said, and would not imply the threat of a steep drain on reserves. It noted that the peso had not fallen two percent in one day since 1995.
